articles.title: 91% OF TOKENIZED STOCKS LEAD BACK TO ONE BROKER
articles.summary: The tokenized stocks market has reached $4.60B, but $4.17B (91%) is backed by shares held at a single US broker, Alpaca Securities, used by seven issuers including Binance bStocks, Ondo, Robinhood, and Coinbase. Those shares sit at DTC under Cede & Co., not under the names of the 4.7M token holders spread across those products. Securitize and Backpack route through RQD Clearing but still terminate at DTC, while only Superstate and Securitize's ISTs hold shares on the issuer's own register, removing both a broker and the depository from the chain. An Alpaca insolvency or regulatory action would put 91% of tokenized equity supply and all 4.7M affected holders at risk from a single counterparty event.

articles.title: COINBASE CEO BACKS TOKENIZING COIN STOCK AS COMPANIES RESIST
articles.summary: Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong backed tokenizing Coinbase shares on X, arguing that restricting new shareholder categories harms the business and that companies should serve customers on the platforms they use. His position contrasts with resistance from 67 companies, including Apple, Tesla, Nvidia, and Meta, that have objected to their shares trading on OKXICE, a joint venture between OKX and Intercontinental Exchange. The objectors represent 56 of OKXICE's 62 original target companies, a 90.3% rejection rate. For tokenized equity platforms, the OKXICE data shows that corporate buy-in, not technical infrastructure, is the binding constraint on stock listings.

articles.title: TEMPO LAUNCHES CREDIT, MATCHING BUSINESSES WITH OUTSIDE LENDERS
articles.summary: Tempo, a payments chain incubated by Stripe and Paradigm, now connects businesses with outside lenders, with draws and repayments settling in stablecoins in under a second, 24/7. Fintechs can borrow for prefunding payouts, receivables, working capital, and consumer credit through a licensed partner. Facilities can have no minimum draw, draws can land as dollars in a bank account and be repaid by wire, and the lender sets terms and takes the risk, not Tempo. The first live case lets eligible El Dorado users in Bolivia borrow USDT from Tala with no collateral.

articles.title: MEZZANINE LAUNCHES RISK-TRANCHED DEFI LOOPING VAULTS
articles.summary: Mezzanine is a DeFi protocol that automates yield looping and splits positions into two risk tranches: Junior (higher yield, first-loss) and Senior (buffered by Junior capital, lower yield). In an 80/20 Senior/Junior split on a 10% APY vault, Senior earns 8% and Junior earns 18%. A 5% drawdown leaves Senior unchanged while Junior absorbs the full loss at a 25% decline. The protocol's first vault, the Hastra Optimizer, accepts USDC or wYLDS and loops Hastra's $PRIME and $AUTO tokens across lending markets backed by US home equity and car loans, with withdrawals taking up to two weeks per epoch. Tranche tokens are composable primitives built for Pendle integration or use as collateral elsewhere, with Mezzanine targeting a role as the structured-risk layer for DeFi looping strategies.

articles.title: KNOW YOUR HUMAN PROTOCOL TO STOP MERCHANTS DECLINING AI AGENT BUYS
articles.summary: Merchants usually decline agent purchases because the agent looks like an unauthorized bot. The video walks through a test: set up an account with KYC and payment details at crypto.sardine.ai, point an agent such as Muse, Instinct, or Dots at the site and watch the purchase fail, then use the same prompt with an agent parameter so Sardine's protocol passes the human's device identifiers and IP to the merchant, and the $30 ETH purchase goes through.

articles.title: VISA LAUNCHES AGENTIC COMMERCE BENCHMARK FOR FRONTIER MODELS
articles.summary: Visa Research published the Visa Agentic Commerce Benchmark, the first public benchmark from a major payments network to evaluate how well frontier models handle autonomous shopping tasks such as price comparison and checkout completion. The release puts Visa Research in the position of defining measurement standards for agentic commerce before those workflows reach production scale.

articles.title: LARGEST ETHENA PAY CARD PAYMENT EARNED UNDER 1% CASHBACK
articles.summary: The biggest Ethena Pay payment since the September 1 launch was $145,271 and earned about $1,180 in cashback. The next largest were $51,435 (about $1,360), $46,014, and $41,255 from one wallet two minutes apart (about $440 combined), $36,263 (about $110), three payments of $27,474.30 from one wallet within 24 hours (about $770 combined), and $26,507 (about $1,050). The rate falls as a wallet spends more each month: VIP earns 5% on the first $20K and 0.5% above $40K, while Standard earns nothing above $4K a month.

articles.title: A NEW MARKET RATE FOR LIQUIDITY: AERODROME
articles.summary: Traditional DEX LP compensation is capped by current swap fee revenue, a constraint that causes liquidity to drain when volume drops, prevents new markets from bootstrapping ahead of organic trading activity, and misaligns tokenholders with LPs. Aerodrome breaks this ceiling by paying LPs in AERO, a token that, when staked, earns a share of total network revenue including dynamic fee premiums, liquidity payments, and MEV capture, so staked AERO yields can exceed any single pool's point-in-time fee output. The token capitalizes claims on future network productivity rather than a fixed fee split, so the protocol can subsidize current liquidity costs at a flexible multiplier as the network grows. Token issuance to LPs transfers future earnings claims from existing holders, and the model holds only when the value the liquidity creates exceeds the dilution issued to attract it.
